left: A 1998 concert review credits cellist Mira Sable as the founder and first director of the Reedglass Quartet, praising the unusually short finale.
right: In a later radio interview, conductor Mira Vale recalls founding the Reedglass Quartet and says her surname was Sable when she led its first season.
rationale: The founding and initial direction of the same quartet identify the musician in both records, and her account connects the two surnames.

left: An inspector's note records that Towpath Stitchworks held a repair class at Birch Exchange on the first Friday in October.
right: A photographer's caption shows the Towpath Stitchworks Cooperative selling kits at Birch Exchange during the annual craft fair.
rationale: The similar names and shared venue are compatible with one group or with separate groups. A repair class and a craft fair supply no distinguishing link.

left: A conservator logged the torn linen of Night Orchard, the painting in Rowan Gallery, while its paper study stayed boxed at Hale Print Archive.
right: The curator at Hale Print Archive mounted Orchard at Night, the paper study for the linen painting held by Rowan Gallery, for a lecture on underdrawing.
rationale: The conservator describes the linen painting and locates the boxed study elsewhere. The curator identifies the other endpoint as that paper study for the painting.

left: The 1971 delivery guide calls Tiller Court the narrow yard reached through the only service arch of Nettle Arcade, with a cobbled loading bay.
right: A modern access survey labels the paved yard beyond the sole service arch of Nettle Arcade The Tiller and measures its turning clearance.
rationale: Both independently locate the yard through the sole service arch of the same arcade. Paving explains the surface change over time.

left: The harbor watch logged the launch Larkswake at Mallow Wharf as it took a towline from Lark, the tug.
right: A crew diary aboard Lark calls it the little tug and records hauling the launch Larkswake away from Mallow Wharf on that morning's tide.
rationale: The harbor watch sees the towed launch receive a line from the tug. The tug crew identifies its own vessel as towing the named launch.

left: A food vendor kept a 2019 receipt for a stall at Lantern Drift, an outdoor lantern gathering behind Sedge Pavilion.
right: A volunteer recalls collecting lanterns after Drift Night behind Sedge Pavilion but cannot place the year.
rationale: The activity, venue and names could describe the same gathering or separate occasions. The volunteer supplies no date or event-specific detail linking the records.

left: The 1962 land register names Narrowbank Reading Room as the grantee on Alder House deed 42Q, recorded with a peppercorn rent.
right: At the library's centenary, a retired secretary recalls accepting the keys when her group signed Alder House deed 42Q as Narrowbank Reading Room, the former name of the Narrowbank Library Trust.
rationale: The recorded grantee of the same numbered deed and the explicit former name identify one institution.

left: A Blue Fan Theatre dresser remembers Len Canter waiting in the wings to go on as the ferryman while his uncle Leon Canter was still conducting below.
right: A Blue Fan Theatre percussionist describes following conductor Leon Canter through the scene where his nephew Len Canter entered as the ferryman.
rationale: Independent backstage and orchestra witnesses distinguish the uncle conducting from the nephew acting during the same scene.

left: A ferry timetable lists Pebblewick Slip in the bend just below Foxmill Bridge, without a street address.
right: A canoe club reminder sends volunteers to Pebblewick Landing next to Three Oars Boathouse, with no description of the surrounding river.
rationale: The records give different landmarks without explaining their relationship. A single landing with two names and two nearby facilities both fit the evidence.

left: The pressroom supervisor remembers labeling a linocut Three Windows immediately before it won the 1984 West Fen Print Prize, after rejecting a smudged proof.
right: The prize juror's diary recalls giving the only 1984 West Fen Print Prize to a large linocut titled Rain Rooms, which the artist had entered under the working title Three Windows.
rationale: The same linocut won the year's sole prize, and the juror connects the working and exhibition titles.

left: The marshal at the Copper Thread Fair held the gate for Spindle Walk at noon while the fair's separate Spindle Stroll was already under way along the canal.
right: A juice vendor at the Copper Thread Fair served Spindle Stroll participants along the canal before heading back to the gate to catch the start of Spindle Walk.
rationale: The marshal and vendor place the two named activities underway at different starting points during the same interval, distinguishing the canal event from the gate event.

left: An old rowing club newsletter calls Thimble its aluminum coaching launch for practice on the Miren Canal.
right: A resident's photo caption calls a yellow work launch The Tin Thimble as it passes Old Tern Lock, with no hull mark readable.
rationale: The similar nicknames could travel with a repainted or repurposed launch. The accounts supply neither a unique match nor evidence of two hulls.

left: A launch-day reporter identifies Heather Swift as the vessel built on Vesper Yard keel 62 and notes that her railings were still unpainted.
right: A docking mechanic records Kite, the vessel built on Vesper Yard keel 62, arriving years later with the earlier name Heather Swift still legible under its stern paint.
rationale: The build identifier links the vessel in the launch report to the later yard visit, and the mechanic can still read the old name.

left: An insurer assigned driver coverage to White Quay Cartage as the loading contractor for the Grain Market relocation and listed White Quay Haulage as a separate insured carrier.
right: A site coordinator assigned unloading to White Quay Haulage on the Grain Market relocation after checking that White Quay Cartage's crew had finished loading.
rationale: The insurer identifies two separately insured firms. The coordinator's account of the handoff identifies the two named crews on opposite sides of the same move.

left: A winter exhibition review describes Frost Line at Plover Rooms as a relief of blue ridges seen through a white frame.
right: A gallery attendant remembers a work called Rimfrost at Plover Rooms with blue ridges inside a white frame but cannot recall the exhibition or artist.
rationale: The titles and visual details are consistent with a translation and the same relief, but neither source identifies a particular installation, artist, or object sufficiently to establish that link.

left: A spectator remembers the Glass Mile as the torch relay that marked the Loomgate viaduct reopening in 1976, with runners finishing on the south ramp.
right: A retired runner says she carried the third torch in the Frost Run, the relay held to mark the Loomgate viaduct reopening in 1976.
rationale: Participants independently identify the relay that marked the same dated reopening, connecting the two informal titles.

left: A volunteer clearing sand from Lower Purl Steps, the public stairs on the east bank, radioed across Purl Footbridge to confirm the west-bank Purl Stair was still closed.
right: Inspectors crossed Purl Footbridge from the open east-bank stairs to examine Purl Stair, the barricaded staircase down the west bank.
rationale: The volunteer and inspectors distinguish two simultaneous stairways at opposite ends of the same crossing and each locates its own endpoint.

left: A rehearsal pianist calls the Buttonwood Opera's 2004 substitute chorus director Rina Orr and recalls that she covered the final week in February.
right: A retired singer calls Katherine Orr the Buttonwood Opera's regular chorus director in the 2004 season and remembers colleagues calling her Rina.
rationale: Katherine's nickname could account for the two names, and a substitute could later become the regular director. Neither witness links the named directors to a specific shared assignment or identifies two separate hires.

left: A deployment note from Darnel Books records the maintainer renaming Tin Ledger to Tallies in its October 2020 release while preserving the existing installation and open ledgers.
right: At Kettle House Museum, a volunteer recalls opening Tin Ledger for inventory after the October 2020 update and finding it titled Tallies with the existing ledgers still open.
rationale: The deployment note and a museum user's observation independently document the same named application's specific update and continuous installation. They describe the change at separate sites.

left: The Wrenline Desktop developer built against the Threadcase C library from Northwick Labs and had to remove the separately imported Threadcase from Hemlock Systems to avoid a symbol collision.
right: Stockroom Viewer maintainers use the Threadcase library from Hemlock Systems and confirm it cannot substitute for the independently shipped Northwick Labs Threadcase C library in their import check.
rationale: Each record identifies its own supplier's library and describes its interaction with the other library. They distinguish two concurrent dependencies, despite the identical display name.

left: The technician at Fallow Annex recorded the Dropfern meter as unit 08 and noted that each field office starts its own unit numbering at 01.
right: Moth Lane Lab photographed a meter marked Dropfern and carrying a unit 08 service sticker, with the issuing field office outside the frame.
rationale: The first witness explains why unit 08 can occur on multiple meters, and the second cannot place the sticker's office. The same name and number neither link nor distinguish physical units.

left: The commissioning technician bolted the custom Spoonbill meter to the Beryl Valve test stand and logged a crescent-shaped gouge beside its lower mounting hole.
right: A safety auditor noted that the meter named Spoonbill still bolted to the Beryl Valve test stand had a crescent-shaped gouge beside the lower mounting hole.
rationale: The custom meter's installed location and the matching shape and precise position of its physical damage jointly identify it across the two inspections.

left: The cloth buyer at the Tansy Trade Fair priced yarn from Aster Thread, the Moss Bank Mill brand, and marked the adjacent Larch Looms Aster Thread label as a separate line on her order card.
right: A Tansy Trade Fair stallholder packed Aster Thread yarn under the Larch Looms label and sent buyers looking for the other Aster Thread brand to the Moss Bank Mill stall.
rationale: The buyer and stallholder independently distinguish two contemporaneous brands sold under the same display name, with separate labels and mill affiliations.

left: At Mica Lane Press, an operator recalls replacing the label-printing tool Felt Desk with a newer app but does not remember what that app was called.
right: An Oriel Lending Library volunteer describes Felt Desk as the label printer that staff installed after a computer move, without identifying its publisher or installation history.
rationale: The press operator observed a switch but never names the replacement. The library witness supplies a name and function on a different installation without evidence linking it to either press application.
